No fender, no problem: Tyler Reddick wins the Autotrader 400, goes back-to-back
item.description: It took 10 cautions, two overtimes and thousands of left turns in 40-degree weather. But in the end, it was 23XI’s racing Tyler Reddick who prevailed at Sunday’s Autotrader 400 at EchoPark Speedway.

item.title: Lady Rams leave region tournament as runner up, Newton boys win third place game
item.description: The Newton Rams left South Gwinnett High School empty-handed on Friday as both teams fell shy of a Region 4-AAAAAA title.The Lady Rams punched their ticket in the final with a 41-35 win on Thursday, but 20-win Archer Lady Tigers did enough to take down the reigning champs, who were without star guard London Smith.Newton’s boys team found themselves in a battle for third place with cross-county rival Rockdale County.

item.title: Leading with Hearts: Local volunteers spend Valentine’s Day serving seniors through Meals on Wheels
item.description: While many celebrated Valentine’s Day with traditional gestures, local community leaders and volunteers chose to honor the day through meaningful service, delivering meals and spreading compassion to elderly residents through a heartfelt Meals on Wheels outreach initiative.

item.title: Georgia Wildlife Federation to host native tree giveaway in Covington
item.description: The Georgia Wildlife Federation will host two native tree giveaways to kick off a year of celebrating its 90th anniversary. Ninety trees will be distributed at the Alcovy Conservation Center in Covington (Newton County) and 90 at Mill Creek Nature Center in Buford (Gwinnett County).

item.title: As Testing Season Nears, Three Years of Data Show Learning Gains in Newton County Classrooms
item.description: As Newton County Schools prepares for upcoming end-of-year state assessments, the district is sharing student performance data since beginning its academic improvement effort three years ago.

item.title: GDOT closing portion of Emory Street for 150 days
item.description: The Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) will soon be closing a portion of State Route 81—where it is locally known as Emory Street—for a five-month bridge replacement project.
